narrator_hint: seventh-storyteller / ending routes: several characters; work out the speaker from context

rows.en:
What, it's my turn now?
I'm feeling rather tired.
I have no particular interest in gatherings like this.
But Hino saw me talking with that child, so I ended up having to come here.
Frankly, I'm in a foul mood.{p}I'd like to go home right now.
Feel free
Please don't go home
This person is scary

Oh, don't make such a flustered face.
Now that I'm here, I'll tell my story.
But I'm in a very foul mood right now.
Keep that firmly in mind.
If this irritation goes on, I might end up killing you.
Heh heh...{p}

I'm Akemi Iwashita, a third-year.
As I said earlier, I'll tell a story about a child.
One about six years old.
Do you find it strange for a child like that to appear in a story about school?{p}

One Sunday, some children sneaked into this school and played hide-and-seek.
And while they played, one little boy hid himself extremely well.{p}

His name was Nao.
The others couldn't figure out where Nao was at all.
So they thought he must have gone home ahead of them, and they left the school.
Nao was left behind all alone.
Even when night came, no one came to find him.
He had no choice but to try to go home, but he couldn't.
Apparently, he hadn't just hidden somewhere hard to find; he had crawled into a place he couldn't get out of on his own.{p}

"Help... somebody... help me...!"
No matter how many times he called, no help came.
That day, his parents grew worried when Nao didn't come home, heard about the hide-and-seek, and came all the way to this school to look for him.
But they couldn't find him either.
Maybe he had been kidnapped...
That's what his parents thought.
So they went to the police, I'm told.
How completely wrong they were.
Nao had no choice but to stay in this school all night long.{p}

The next day, and the day after that, he couldn't get out of his hiding place.
The students, the teachers, the janitor... not a single person found Nao.
...You can guess the rest by now, can't you?
In time, Nao starved to death.{p}Well, {a}?
If you were that child, could you simply pass on in peace?
I could
I couldn't
I'd imagine not.{p}

Actually, Nao's body was never found.
Where it lay remained a mystery, too.
And do you know why?
Let's see... Say, for example, that you found Nao's body.
Then, out of nowhere, you would hear a little boy's voice.
"So now I'm it?
Then it's your turn to hide."
Once you hear that, it's all over.
You'll be shut in that place, and you'll never get out again.
Naturally, all that's left for you is to die.{p}

Heh heh... Interesting, isn't it?
If it were true, there must be bodies lying all over that place, or so my classmates were clamoring.
Where do you think a place like that might be?
This school is big, and there are any number of suspicious spots.
It could be a storeroom, or it could be a classroom no one uses anymore.
Or perhaps it's the old school building.
As a matter of fact, hunting for it was all the rage for a while.
That was back when I had just started here.{p}

There was a boy in my class named Nao Aoki.
He was cheerful and easygoing, and he quickly became everyone's favorite.
Everyone was always calling his name, "Nao, Nao."
His seat was next to mine, and there were always a bunch of classmates swarming around it.{p}

At times like that, Nao would sometimes talk to me.
He'd urge me to join the conversation, or ask if I wanted to stop somewhere with everyone after school.
Frankly, he was a nuisance.
I prefer being alone, after all.{p}

Then one day, a girl in our class came in having heard, from somewhere, the rumor about the child who died at school.
...After that, the story started catching on in my class.
Did the boy who died playing hide-and-seek really exist?
Where was he hiding?
Were there really people who found the child's body and died?
If there were, how many of them?
And what drew the most attention was the idea of finding the boy's body and testing whether you could make it home alive.{p}

Saying they would find Nao, the dead child, a few of my classmates sneaked into the school on a Sunday.
There was some rumor that made little sense: since the child got lost at school on a Sunday, Sunday was the best day to look for him, too.{p}

Me?
Of course I didn't take part in anything like that.{p}Well, {a}?
Are you the type who would enjoy that sort of thing?
I'd enjoy it and try it myself
I'd only listen to the stories
I'm not interested

I see...
You look to me like quite the type to enjoy it, though.
Well, isn't it obvious?
You joined the newspaper club because you're the type who wants to poke your nose into everything, didn't you?
That's the feeling I get.{p}

"Some unwholesome game seems to be popular lately, but stop going into off-limits areas on Sundays."
One day, the school, unable to ignore what everyone was doing any longer, gave us a warning.
The year head came to our classroom, and it caused a huge fuss.
He said ours was about the only class doing such things, and gave us quite a lecture.{p}

But nobody stopped searching.
I suppose the thrill of searching in secret only made it better.
The searches escalated more and more.
There were accidents now and then, too: someone got hurt when a shelf in the old school building collapsed, someone cut a hand on glass trying to break open a door that wouldn't budge.{p}

...It was then that something happened.
One of the classmates who had taken part in the searches went missing.
The hunt for the child's body could no longer be passed off as a game.
Where had the missing student gone?
Going to the police would make it a big affair, so it was decided that we would all look into it ourselves first.{p}{a}, which place do you think is suspicious?
The old school building
Some storeroom somewhere
The roof
That's right.{p}

Everyone thought the old school building was the suspicious place.
So, with the year head supervising, our whole class was given permission to go inside.
We split into teams of two and searched for the student from the morning on.
I ended up on the same team as Nao.
Simply because our seats were next to each other.{p}

...Once inside the old school building, Nao opened some random classroom and sat down on a chair.
I sat down too, without a word.
I didn't particularly feel like walking around anyway.
We stayed there, still, listening to the sounds of a P.E. class drifting in from the schoolyard... whistles and chatter, and the sound of the wind.
I could tell he was gazing at my profile every so often.
I was somewhat tired, so I didn't complain about it.
"Iwashita... I..."
He started to say something.{p}

Just then, out of nowhere, I heard what sounded like a scream.
Then the old school building grew noisy somehow.
It seemed the missing student had been found.
The moment that happened, Nao stood up.
What had become of the missing student?
Judging from the strange atmosphere inside the old school building, I thought there was no way he was all right.
It wouldn't be bad to see how someone who'd played such a stupid game ended up.
I went out into the hallway with Nao.{p}

Still, it was strange.
For a new student, Nao walked as if he knew his way around the old school building.
He strode ahead on his own, without a moment's hesitation.
"Ah!"
He was walking so fast that I tripped along the way and fell against the wall.
I scraped my hand when I did.{p}

Nao lent me his handkerchief.
"Sorry. I got in too much of a hurry..."
I had a handkerchief of my own, of course.
But I didn't want to get it dirty.
And it was his fault I'd nearly fallen.
So I used his without a word.{p}

Nao started walking again.
And he made it all the way to the scene.
Even though he hadn't asked anyone where the missing student had been found.
When I asked him how, Nao gave a vague answer, something like "I just had a feeling."
...And then he stopped in front of a certain room.{p}

When Nao opened the door, the missing boy was inside.
He was sprawled out, arms and legs bent at odd angles, groaning in pain.
There was a big hole in the floor beside him.
It looked like he had fallen through it and broken some bones.
Eyes wide open, he was grinding his head against the wooden floor, squirming pathetically.{p}

An ambulance was called right away.
Still, it's remarkable how Nao went straight to that room without losing his way even once.{p}Don't you think so?
Yes, I think so
No, I don't

...The student with the broken bones was taken away by ambulance without further trouble.
When they put him on the stretcher, it must have hurt terribly, because he let out a horrendous scream.
It was disgusting to watch.
In the end, it was put down as an accident caused by his own carelessness.
And once again, the year head gave us a lecture.
A very long one, too.{p}

And then, after school that day.
The year head called Nao in.
It seemed the two of them were going to talk about something in the guidance office.
I had absolutely no interest in what they talked about, but I had to return the handkerchief Nao had lent me.
So I waited outside the guidance office for a while.
I wanted to give back the handkerchief and go home quickly, but the two of them talked on and on.
Weren't they going to finish anytime soon?
I quietly peeked in through the gap in the door.{p}

Then I could just make out the conversation inside.
"So you're the culprit, aren't you?"
...It was the year head's voice.
"Sir, why would you say that?"
"I'm the one who should be asking why.
You're the one who spread that rumor about the child who died playing hide-and-seek, aren't you?"
"...Yes... I suppose I am."
What was going on?
Puzzled, I kept listening closely for a while.
The hide-and-seek story was one a girl in our class had picked up from somewhere.
And yet Nao was the one who spread it?
Maybe he first told someone in another class, then waited for the rumor to spread back to his own.
Still, it was odd.
People in other classes knew the story too, so why had the body hunt caught on so much in our class alone...?
Just then, a thought came to me.{p}

What if Nao had set it all up?
The class favorite, who always kept people gathered in attendance around his desk... making some topic catch on would have been child's play for him, wouldn't it?{p}But... why?
Why would he need to do something like that?
To get his classmates hurt
To make trouble for the year head

Oh... is that what you think, {a}?
Heh heh, I wonder if what's in your head really matches the truth.{p}
Well, never mind. I'll go on with the story.{p}

...The year head stood up and grabbed Nao by the arm.
It looked pretty rough.
Nao seemed to be in pain.
"Aoki, you're the one who broke that classmate's bones in the old school building too, aren't you?"
"That's not true, sir."
The conversation was heading in a more and more sinister direction.
The year head and Nao kept glaring at each other.
The silence dragged on.{p}
It was the year head who broke it.{p}

"Why did you give the child who played hide-and-seek the same name as yours?"
Then Nao suddenly broke into a grin.
"Now you've slipped up, sir."
"Wh-what do you mean?"
"The child in that story never had a name to begin with, right?
But I'd think the only one who knows that is the man from that day..."
"So you really were that brat!★"{p}

The year head's eyes flew wide open.
Then, without warning, he punched Nao.
"Sir, are you going to kill me too?
Like that child back then..."
"Yeah, that's right. I'll kill you too!
Listen, I'm married to her now, and I'm happy.
I won't let anybody get in my way!☆"
The teacher straddled Nao and punched him in the face again and again.
And yet Nao kept on grinning.
"Sir, stop wasting your effort.
I can see it.
On your shoulders..."
"What?!★"{p}
...A horrible sound rang out.{p}

The child's ghost took the teacher, his mouth hanging open and his eyes gone blank, and threw him out the open window.
Students screamed outside, and a commotion broke out.
...After that, the child's ghost began wandering around all alone.
"Mommy... where...?"
That's what it was saying.
It spoke to Nao, who was right in front of it.
"Do you know where Mommy is?"
Nao said nothing.
So the child came toward the door I was peeking through.{p}
Suddenly the door was flung open.{p}

"Ah..."
"Hey, miss, do you know where Mommy is?"
"......"
I said nothing, too.
After all, I knew nothing about that child's mother.
But Nao knew the whole story.
That's what I thought.{p}

...The child's ghost started to wander unsteadily down the hallway.
Head hanging, utterly dejected.
Kind of pitiful
That's scary
I wonder where it's going

"Iwashita! What are you doing here?"
He came straight out into the hallway.
"I came to return your handkerchief."
"...I see.
Still... I'm glad. Glad no harm came to you too."
He was gasping for breath, his shoulders heaving.
He was acting tough, but maybe he'd been scared after all.
Then, wheezing, he started following the child's ghost.
He said there had to be a body wherever it was going.
I wanted to know what this was all about.
So I decided to go with him.
As Nao followed the child, he slowly told me everything.{p}

...When he was little, he once snuck into this school to play.
He crept into the old school building as a prank and wandered all over the place.{p}

That was when he found the body of a small child in a hole in a classroom floor.
The same hole our classmate fell into and broke his bones.
While Nao was panicking, the one who had killed the child came along.
Carrying planks of wood to cover up the hole in the floor.{p}

That killer was the year head.
Back then he must have been a new teacher, I suppose.
To keep Nao from telling anyone about the body, the teacher cleverly talked him around.
There's a story about a child who died playing hide-and-seek.
If you see that body, then it's your turn to die.{p}

If he had said he'd seen it, the teacher might have killed Nao right then and there.
And after sending Nao home, the teacher hid the child's body somewhere else.{p}

...Nao, for his part, believed every word the teacher said.
Even after he got home, he kept telling himself:
I didn't see it.
I didn't see anything.
Nao tried desperately to forget the whole thing.
Well, he was only a little boy, after all.
As he grew up, he really did manage to forget.{p}

But when he came to our school, something nagged at him.
He had seen this place before.
But whenever he tried to remember, his head began to ache.
What could it mean...?{p}

It was around then that Nao saw the ghost of a small child, he said.
The child was saying,
"Mommy... where...?"
as it wandered unsteadily near the old school building.{p}

And that was when Nao remembered.
The story of the child who died playing hide-and-seek.
Finding the body.
And last of all, the frightening man.
Once you're in high school, of course, you can tell there was something fishy about that man.{p}

Nao gave the dead child the same name as his own and spread the rumor on purpose.
He figured that if the frightening man heard the story, he would surely make some kind of move against him.{p}

Tell me, {a}.
Do you want to know why the year head killed that child?
I want to know
I don't want to know

There was a woman the year head wanted to marry.
She had a child, and she was raising it on her own.
The father wasn't around at the time.
I don't know what the circumstances were.
In any case, she kept balking at marrying the year head.
She must be worried about her child.
That's what the year head thought.
The child was in the way.
If only it would just disappear.
He thought that, too.{p}

So he secretly killed her child, you see.
Luring the child out was easy.
He said the school where he worked was huge, and he'd take the child there to play.
Of course, he kept the whole thing from the mother.
Then he took the child to the old school building and killed it.{p}

...While I was listening to all this, we reached the back garden near the old school building.
The trees and grass there are hardly ever tended, so it's like being up in the mountains, isn't it?
Deep in that back garden, the child's ghost crouched down.
It cried "Mommy, Mommy" for a while, and then it fell asleep, as if worn out.{p}

"...The body must be buried right here.
Hey, Iwashita, do you think we should tell the mother about this child?"
That's what Nao asked me.{p}{a}, what would you have answered?
You should tell her
Better not to tell her
I don't know

I see...
I wouldn't know.{p}

I don't know whether we should tell her or not.
I can't say what's right.
It's just that I had no intention of telling her.
I mean, what a bother.
And it's not as if I owed her that.{p}

When I said nothing, Nao spoke.
"Why don't we keep this a secret?"
he said.
"Let's not tell anyone the year head killed the child, either.
I mean, think how awful it'd be for the mother.
Her child murdered, and her husband a criminal..."
Of course, I had no reason to object.{p}
I was about to tell him that was fine, when he came out with this.{p}

"...And also... about what I started to say in the old school building earlier."
"What?"{p}

"The truth is, Iwashita, I've had my eye on you for a while now."
"What do you mean?"
"Well... if you're okay with it, I'd like you to go out with me."
...You've got to be joking.
I had found him annoying all along.
You could even call him an eyesore.
I changed the subject right away.
I asked about something that had been bothering me.
"Come to think of it, the year head said something strange, didn't he?
That you were the one who broke the missing student's bones, Nao..."{p}

Nao said that wasn't true.
He said the year head must have done it to scare us.
But that's strange, isn't it?
The year head seemed to genuinely not know.
Which left only one other possible culprit...{p}
When I happened to look, the child's ghost had crept up behind Nao.{p}
The ghost laid its hand on his arm, and there was a dull crack.{p}

"Gyaaaaah!☆"
Nao screamed.
He dropped to his knees on the ground, clutching his arm in agony.
"Help me, Iwashi... Hel...!"{p}

Then came the sound of another bone breaking.
His leg, this time.
He looked just like the missing student had with his broken bones.
That was when I understood.
The missing student broke his bones because he went poking around the place where the child died, just for fun.
And Nao's bones were broken probably because he said we should keep the child a secret from its mother...{p}

Once the child's ghost had broken every one of Nao's arms and legs, it turned toward me.
"Miss."
Its voice was innocent.
"Where's Mommy?"
I took a breath and answered.
"...I don't know."
"......"{p}

The child trudged off somewhere.
...And Hino had seen the whole thing.
When I told him what had happened, he asked if he could use it as material someday.
Nao transferred to another school soon after.
I suppose he was scared of the child's ghost.{p}

In the end, the year head's death was written off as a suicide with no known cause.
Because neither Nao nor I explained anything to the police.
Even if we had tried, they wouldn't have believed us.
Hm? The child's mother?
Who knows... I have no idea what became of her.
That child is still at this school, though, searching for its mother.
It wanders around near the old school building now and then.
I suppose I could dig through the old rosters and look into the year head's wife for it.
But I don't care to go that far.
I'd rather not stick my nose in too deep.{p}

Are you trying to make me angry?
I haven't even told my story yet, and you say I can go home? What is that supposed to mean?
If you say anything that stupid again, I'll kill you.
Hino spent days persuading me before I agreed to come.
Do you intend to let all his trouble go to waste?
He must be so happy to have such a wonderful junior.{p}

Heh heh...
I knew it.
You seem like that sort.
Aren't you the type who meddles where you're not wanted and tramples into other people's privacy without a second thought?
What a troublesome person.
Well, I suppose it's fine, as long as you enjoy yourself.
But you'd better be very careful.
Nao went through something terrible because of this search.{p}

He wasn't the type to get a kick out of rumors.
But you see, he just couldn't stop thinking about how the child everyone was talking about had the same name as him.
His classmates said it was probably a coincidence.
But every Sunday, Nao went searching all over for the child's body.{p}

And he was the very first one to find it.
In a classroom in the old school building.
The wooden floor there has rotted away in places, leaving holes.
The child's body was lying inside one of those holes.
"Aww, you found me."
Suddenly, he heard a voice behind him.{p}

It was a child with the same face as the body.
Could it be... a ghost...?
He'd never dreamed the story was actually true.
Nao panicked.
But no sound came out of his mouth.
As if he were paralyzed, he couldn't move a single step.
"Now I'm it, mister. It's your turn to hide."
With that, the child melted into the air and vanished.{p}

At that very moment, the door slammed shut.
It made such a loud noise that it seemed it might break.
Nao ran straight to the door.
But it would not open, no matter what he did.
"Somebody! Somebody!"
He pounded on the door desperately, but no one came.
Just like the child who had died there, he called for help again and again.
...His throat grew raw, and his voice went hoarse.
He felt as if he might start coughing up blood.
But still, no help came.{p}

He couldn't go home that whole night.
Just when he thought he would never get out of there for the rest of his life...{p}

The boy's ghost appeared again.
"You're so noisy, mister, I found you.
That's no good. You're supposed to hide quietly."
And then the door opened.
Nao fled as fast as he could.
He swore he would never go near the old school building again.
As Nao ran, the child murmured at his back,
"Now you're it, mister."{p}Well, {a}?
Do you think Nao took his turn as 'it' and went looking for that child again?
He went looking for the child
He didn't go looking

Heh heh...
That's right.
There's no reason to go out of your way to see a child like that, is there?
Nao tried to forget all about it.{p}

...And a few days went by.
His classmates kept up their search as usual.
With all this searching, why hadn't anyone found that classroom?
True, that hole in the floor was dark and hard to spot, but...
Nao found it eerie.
But he couldn't bring himself to tell anyone what he'd been through.
It had all been a bad dream.
Maybe that's what he wanted to believe.{p}

Then one day, that boy appeared before Nao again.
It was during class.
Someone tapped him on the shoulder from behind, and when he turned around, the child was riding on his shoulders.
The child was glaring at Nao with a terrifying look in its eyes.
"Why won't you come look for me?
I've been waiting this whole time.
You're it, mister.
You have to come and find me!"
Nao stared at the child, unable to move.{p}

"Hey, where do you think you're looking?"
The teacher scolded him.
Apparently the teacher couldn't see the child's ghost.
And not only the teacher.
Not one of his classmates could see the child's ghost either.
"H-help me..."
Nao forced the words out.
But everyone laughed.
They thought he had said it because the teacher had scolded him.
Why is everyone laughing?
Don't they care what happens to me?
Unable to bear it any longer, he ran out of the classroom.{p}

Before he knew it, Nao found himself near the old school building.
No way.
He had no intention of going in there, he thought.
But the ghost's small hands pulled him by the hair and dragged him into the old school building.
Its strength was tremendous.
It was as if the child's obsession were being thrust before his eyes.{p}

"I'm getting bored of this game..."
Well, Nao was overjoyed.
Without thinking, he started to smile at it, and the ghost's hand shot out at him.
It was so sudden that Nao couldn't think at all.
He staggered helplessly under the push, and fell into the hole in the floor.{p}

The next day, he let out the shrillest scream he could, so that someone would hear.
He yelled again and again, over and over.
Even when his voice gave out, he rested only a little, then kept on screaming.
{a}, can you imagine that?
To anyone hearing it from outside, how horrifying that voice must have sounded.
Eventually, a student who heard the screams called a teacher.
Nao was rescued, and he frantically told them everything that had happened.
They say he wept and wailed that he was going to move away somewhere.
And what became of him... can you guess?{p}

He got put in a hospital.
People said he must have been wandering around in a daze, fallen into the hole, and hit his head or something.
At first Nao couldn't accept that, but he thought getting away from school wasn't such a bad thing.
He wanted to go somewhere the child's ghost couldn't see him.
For a while, he stayed quietly in the hospital.
But then, two or three days later...{p}

One night, Nao woke up suddenly and saw someone crouching in a corner of his hospital room.
It was a small child.{p}"Are you sick, mister?"
The voice sounded terribly lonely.
He says he's sick
He says he's not sick

"No... I'm not really sick.
What's the matter with you, kid?
Which room are you from?"
Nao answered timidly.
Could this child be...?
Has the child I met at school followed me here?
With that fear weighing on him, Nao waited for an answer.
"You're not sick?
That's a relief.
But then why did you go home in the middle of hide-and-seek?
I looked for you everywhere!"
When he heard those words, everything went black before Nao's eyes.{p}

...He's in the old school building.
I'm not lying.
I saw the child's ghost dragging Nao there with my own eyes.
When I asked what it was doing, the child smiled sweetly and said they were playing hide-and-seek.{p}

The child started telling me all about it, having a wonderful time.
How well it had hidden.
How good it was at finding people who hid.
How it had dragged Nao back, even when he'd gone to hide outside the school, and so on.
More or less what I've been telling you.
And Hino saw me then, you see.
He asked me to let him write it up as an article someday.{p}

He calls it an interview, and then holds a get-together like some kind of round-table discussion.
I hate doing things in groups.
So I want no part of this sort of thing.
But Hino is persistent, isn't he?
He kept insisting, so this time I was forced into taking part.
It really puts me in a foul mood.{p}

Oh, yes. It seems Nao was taken to the classroom where the child died.
Inside the hole in that classroom's floor, the two Naos must be getting along nicely.
One in the form of a child.
The other in the form of a high school student.
It seems the two of them having the same name was pure coincidence.
The one to pity is the high school Nao.
He was never the type to stick his nose into strange rumors to begin with...{p}

If anything, {a}, isn't it people like you, who get a kick out of rumors, who ought to meet that kind of fate?
Heh heh...
Go to the old school building sometime, if you feel like it.
The two Naos might let you join their game of hide-and-seek.{p}...That's the end of my story.
Now, the fifth one is next.
What kind of story will you tell us this time?{p}

Heh heh...
Does that mean that's what you would do?
Oh, please. If you did that, you would have to play hide-and-seek with the child's ghost forever.
That might be fine for you, but Nao thought differently.
He tried to forget all about it.{p}

"You know, I used to hurt all over, and get hungry, but now I'm fine.
Hey, mister, you should become just like me."
The child's cold hand touched Nao.
"Then we can play hide-and-seek together forever..."{p}

...They say that the next day, Nao was found dead in his hospital room.
Apparently there was quite a fuss over it, with talk of psychological shock.
The truth is, Nao had an older brother who went missing as a small child.
Supposedly he went out to play one day and never came back...{p}

The child's body in the old school building belonged to that older brother.
After losing their child, the parents gave Nao, who was born later, the same name as his brother.
